Describe a photo

Choose a photo you like and write about it in English.

1
Choose a photo.From the list, from the Internet, or one of your own photos.
2
Write it by hand.At least 35 words in your notebook. Write the photo number at the top (for example: Photo 7).
3
Submit it.Take a clear photo of your text. Upload it to Google Classroom.
This work will be marked!  Deadline: Thursday 19/11, midnight

Use the phrases

Two phrases together ✌️

There’s a palm tree in the top-right corner.

Present continuous = what is happening now

I am + verb-ing
He / She / It is + verb-ing
They / We / You are + verb-ing

Short: He’s · She’s · They’re · I’m

✗ He holding a sign.
✓ He’s holding a sign.
✗ They running.
✓ They’re running.

Don’t forget am / is / are! 💡

Always true → present simple: He has long hair. (NOT He’s having)

Adjectives go before a noun (a beautiful, sunny day) or after be, look, seem (It’s sunny. She looks happy. He seems friendly).
a sunny day  ·  It’s sunny.  ·  She looks happy.  ·  two big trees (NOT bigs)  ·  long blonde hair

Try it! Which is right?

and → more information
She’s smiling and she looks happy.
but → something different
She has long hair, but he has short hair.
so → the result
It’s sunny, so they’re at the beach.
because → the reason
He’s smiling because he’s happy.
or → one or the other
I think it’s a park or a garden.
OK: John is standing on the left. He is smiling.
BETTER: John is standing on the left, and he is smiling.

How your teacher will mark your work

Marking criteria

What?Very GoodMuito Bom · 18–20GoodBom · 14–17SatisfactorySuficiente · 10–13InsufficientInsuficiente · 0–9
1. The task5 parts · at least 35 words · 20 points All 5 parts. 35 words or more. The text describes the photo clearly. 4 or 5 parts. 35 words or more. 3 parts, or the text is too short (25–34 words). Fewer than 3 parts or fewer than 25 words. The text is not about the photo.
2. Where?There is / There are · places · prepositions · 20 points There is / There are are correct. 2 or more place phrases (on the left, in the background, next to…). Two phrases together: at the top, on the left. There is / There are + 1 or 2 place phrases. Few mistakes. Tries There is / There are or place phrases, with some mistakes. No There is / There are and no place phrases.
3. What is happening?present continuous: am / is / are + -ing · 20 points 2 or more correct sentences: He’s holding… They’re walking… 1 or 2 sentences with small mistakes. Uses -ing, but sometimes forgets am / is / are (They walking). No present continuous.
4. Adjectivespeople · things · places · 20 points 3 or more adjectives in the right place: long blonde hair, a sunny day, She looks happy. 2 adjectives, mostly correct. 1 adjective, or mistakes like bigs trees / a day sunny. No adjectives.
5. Joining words & accuracyand · but · or · so · because · spelling · 20 points Joins ideas with and / but / so / because. Very few spelling or punctuation mistakes. Uses and or because. Some mistakes, but the text is clear. Only short sentences. Many mistakes, but we can understand it. Very difficult to understand.

5 criteria × 20 points = 100 points

Very Good 90–100Good 70–89Satisfactory 50–69Insufficient 0–49

✍️ More than 50 words is OK – but fewer than 35 words loses points.
